label: Unit classes
description: What kind of body the player controls. The six generator classes come from the brief; 'naval' is kept for research only.

terms.label: Infantry
terms.description: A soldier on foot, from rifleman to power-suit trooper or war animal. Small hitbox, uses cover, can enter vehicles and buildings.

terms.label: Tank / ground vehicle
terms.description: A wheeled or tracked ground vehicle: buggies, tanks, IFVs and APCs, artillery. This is the brief's 'tank' class, widened so IFVs and buggies fit.

terms.label: Walker / mech
terms.description: A vehicle on legs, from a nimble scout walker to a towering assault mech. Steps over low obstacles and has a strong silhouette.

terms.label: Hovercraft
terms.description: Rides on an air cushion or anti-grav field, so it crosses land and water. Slides and drifts when it turns.

terms.label: Aircraft
terms.description: A crewed flyer: helicopter, VTOL, jet or airship. Ignores ground obstacles; a top-down view needs a clear height cue such as a shadow.

terms.label: Drone / support
terms.description: A small uncrewed machine or support device: attack, scout and repair drones and deployable gadgets. Usually fast and fragile; the player is the machine.
terms.notes: Only for uncrewed units of tiny or small size; bigger robots are classed by how they move. Support is a role, not a class: a repair truck is a vehicle with the support role.

terms.label: Naval (research only)
terms.description: Ships and submarines. Recorded only when they teach a mechanic, such as submerging. The generator never rolls this class.
